title: Functorial support-quotient pullback maps and site comparison
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Work with ordinary module sheaves over the constant ring sheaves $A_T$ on small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. For a closed immersion $a:C\hookrightarrow T$ of schemes whose open complement $j:T\setminus C\hookrightarrow T$ is quasi-compact [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], put
$$Q^\tau_{T,C}=\operatorname{coker}(j_!A_{T\setminus C}\to A_T),\qquad r^\tau_{T,C}:A_T\twoheadrightarrow Q^\tau_{T,C},\quad\tau=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet},$$
where the arrow is the open-inclusion map and $j_!$ is extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Let $f:T'\to T$ be a scheme morphism and $a':C'\hookrightarrow T'$ another such closed immersion, with quasi-compact open complement, such that $f\circ a'$ factors through $a$. Use constant-coefficient module pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. In each topology there is a unique module morphism
$$c^\tau_{f;C,C'}:f^*Q^\tau_{T,C}\longrightarrow Q^\tau_{T',C'}\quad\text{with}\quad c^\tau_{f;C,C'}\circ f^*r^\tau_{T,C}=r^\tau_{T',C'},$$
under the canonical identification $f^*A_T\cong A_{T'}$. In the etale topology its stalk is the identity $A\to A$ on $C'$ and the zero map to zero off $C'$. If $C'=T'\times_TC$ as a closed subscheme [def-pc-fibre-product], this morphism is an isomorphism in both topologies. These morphisms are identities for identity maps of pairs and satisfy
$$c^\tau_{f\circ g;C,C''}=c^\tau_{g;C',C''}\circ g^*c^\tau_{f;C,C'}$$
for $g:T''\to T'$ carrying $C''$ into $C'$, assuming all three complements quasi-compact, under the canonical inverse-image composition comparisons.

Let $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and let $\alpha_{T,C}:\nu_T^*Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}\xrightarrow{\sim}Q^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}$ be the comparison carrying $\nu_T^*r^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}$ to $r^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}$ [lem-pur-support-quotient-flat]. Then, under $\nu_{T'}^*f_{\mathrm{et}}^*\cong f_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\nu_T^*$ [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback],
$$c^{\mathrm{proet}}_{f;C,C'}\circ f_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\alpha_{T,C}=\alpha_{T',C'}\circ\nu_{T'}^*c^{\mathrm{et}}_{f;C,C'}.$$
All asserted composition and comparison compatibilities are equalities of ordinary sheaf morphisms. Neither flatness of $f$ nor reducedness of the closed supports is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03Q1, label lemma-stalk-pullback, especially (1) and (3); agent-formulated support-quotient functoriality refinement with the normalized etale/pro-etale comparisons of the blueprint, not an assertion attributed to this tag alone.

proof.text:
Work first on the etale sites. Write $U=T\setminus C$, $U'=T'\setminus C'$, and $b:j_!A_U\to A_T$ for the defining open-inclusion arrow. The category of constant-ring module sheaves is abelian, with cokernels obtained by sheafifying sectionwise cokernels. By exactness of constant-coefficient module pullback, the sequence
$$f_{\mathrm{et}}^*j_!A_U\xrightarrow{f^*b} A_{T'}\xrightarrow{f^*r^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}}f_{\mathrm{et}}^*Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}\to0$$
is a cokernel presentation, using the constant-section-preserving identification $f^*A_T\cong A_{T'}$. In particular $f^*r^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}$ is an epimorphism.

source.place: Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (1); constant-ring module version of Tag 04JC, sites-modules.tex lemma-flat-pullback-exact

proof.text:
The composite $h=r^{\mathrm{et}}_{T',C'}\circ f^*b$ is zero. Indeed, at a geometric point $\bar x'$ in $C'$, the image $\bar x=f\bar x'$ lies in $C$, by the assumed factorization of $fa'$ through $a$. The inverse-image stalk isomorphism and extension-by-zero stalk formula give
$$(f^*j_!A_U)_{\bar x'}\cong(j_!A_U)_{\bar x}=0.$$
At a geometric point outside $C'$ the target stalk $(Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T',C'})_{\bar x'}$ is zero by the support-quotient stalk formula. Thus every stalk of $h$ is zero. For completeness, exact stalk functors carry the abelian-sheaf image of $h$ to its zero stalk image; conservativity applied to $0\to\operatorname{im}(h)$ makes this image zero, hence $h=0$. This argument is on underlying abelian sheaves and therefore also proves the equality of module morphisms.

source.place: Tags 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact), 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks); extension-by-zero stalk description in proposition-describe-jshriek

proof.text: The cokernel universal property applied to $h=0$ gives the unique $A_{T'}$-linear map $c^{\mathrm{et}}_{f;C,C'}$ satisfying the stated equation. On a geometric stalk in $C'$, the source and target quotient stalks are both $A$, and both quotient maps in that equation are the identity of $A$. Here the source identification uses the natural inverse-image stalk isomorphism, which carries pulled-back constant germs to the same constant germs. Hence the stalk of $c^{\mathrm{et}}$ is $\operatorname{id}_A$. Outside $C'$ its target is zero and its stalk is the unique map to zero (the source can be $A$ or zero).

proof.text: If $C'=T'\times_TC$, a geometric point of $T'$ lies in $C'$ exactly when its image lies in $C$. The stalks of $f^*Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}$ and $Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T',C'}$ are therefore simultaneously $A$ or zero. The map computed in the preceding step is respectively $\operatorname{id}_A$ or the unique isomorphism $0\to0$. Geometric-stalk conservativity gives that $c^{\mathrm{et}}_{f;C,C'}$ is an isomorphism. This uses the actual fiber product of the closed immersions, and does not assert that a morphism factors through a closed subscheme merely from inclusion of its image.

u_T^*A_T$, each adjoint to a constant-section map and so carrying the pulled-back constant section $a$ to the constant section $a$. For $a\in A$ the constant section is a map $a:*	o A_T$, and naturality gives $ho_{f,A_T}\circ
u_{T'}^*f_{\mathrm{et}}^*(a)=f_{\mathrm{proet}}^*

Thus the transported $ho_{f,A_T}$ is an endomorphism of $A_{T'}$ fixing every constant section; as $A_{T'}$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf, the universal property of sheafification makes it the identity. The same argument applies to every natural isomorphism between composites of these finite-product-preserving functors, in particular to the identity and composition comparisons on either site, so they respect the coefficient identifications; on the pro-etale site this is the equation of lem-pur-proetale-constant-ring-composition. proof.text:
Now define the pro-etale map by the actual composite of ordinary module morphisms
$$c^{\mathrm{proet}}_{f;C,C'}=\alpha_{T',C'}\circ
u_{T'}^*(c^{\mathrm{et}}_{f;C,C'})\circho_{f,Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}}^{-1}\circ(f_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\alpha_{T,C})^{-1}.$$
The normalization $\alpha\circ
u^*r^{\mathrm{et}}=r^{\mathrm{proet}}$, naturality of $ho_f$ at $r^{\mathrm{et}}$, and its coefficient normalization just checked give $c^{\mathrm{proet}}\circ f_{\mathrm{proet}}^*r^{\mathrm{proet}}=r^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T',C'}$. Moreover $f_{\mathrm{proet}}^*r^{\mathrm{proet}}$ is, through these same isomorphisms, $
u_{T'}^*(f_{\mathrm{et}}^*r^{\mathrm{et}})$. The latter is an epimorphism because the module comparison functor is exact. Thus precomposition with $f_{\mathrm{proet}}^*r^{\mathrm{proet}}$ is injective on morphisms and proves uniqueness on the pro-etale site. Multiplying the displayed defining formula by $f_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\alpha_{T,C}$ on the right gives precisely the required site-comparison square under $ho_f$.

proof.text: In the Cartesian-support case the etale map was proved to be an isomorphism. Its image under $\nu_{T'}^*$ is an isomorphism (a functor sends an inverse to an inverse), and every other factor in the displayed formula for $c^{\mathrm{proet}}$ is an isomorphism. Their composite is therefore an isomorphism as well.

proof.text:
For an identity map of pairs, the identity of $Q^\tau_{T,C}$ satisfies the defining quotient equation, so uniqueness gives the identity assertion in each topology. For $T''\xrightarrow gT'\xrightarrow fT$, use the canonical inverse-image composition comparison, whose coefficient normalization was checked above. Precomposing the proposed composite with $(f\circ g)^*r^\tau_{T,C}$ gives
$$c^\tau_{g;C',C''}\circ g^*(c^\tau_{f;C,C'}\circ f^*r^\tau_{T,C})=c^\tau_{g;C',C''}\circ g^*r^\tau_{T',C'}=r^\tau_{T'',C''}.$$
The pair condition is transitive, since the two given factorizations compose. Uniqueness for the pair $(f\circ g;C,C'')$ proves the composition equation. These are equalities of ordinary sheaf morphisms: no derived or stalkwise equality is substituted for the asserted equalities. Quasi-compactness is used only to keep all the support quotients and their comparisons within the hypotheses of lem-pur-support-quotient-flat; no flatness of a scheme morphism or reducedness assumption was used.
